content: I'll read the test image to classify the plant disease.

**Analysis of the test image:**

**Affected plant part:** Banana fruits (two bananas shown)

**Key visual features observed:**
- Large, irregular dark black/brown necrotic spots scattered across the yellow banana peel (upper fruit)
- The lower banana shows severely progressed disease with extensive confluent dark lesions covering most of the fruit surface
- Spots appear sunken and irregular in shape
- Yellow background with distinct dark brown-to-black lesion coloration
- Progressive tissue decay pattern consistent with fungal infection

**Matching against classes:**

| Class | Fit |
|---|---|
| **Anthracnose** | Strong match — *Colletotrichum musae* causes exactly these dark, irregular, sunken spots on banana fruit surfaces, particularly during and after ripening |
| Cigar_End_Rot | Affects only the blossom/tip end of the fruit, not distributed across the surface |
| Cordana_Leaf_Spot | A leaf disease — oval brown spots on leaves, not on fruit |
| Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka | A leaf disease — streaks/spots on leaves |
| Bunchy_Top | Viral disease affecting plant architecture/leaf arrangement, not fruit |
| Panama_Disease | Fusarium wilt — causes internal stem/vascular discoloration and leaf wilt, not fruit surface lesions |

**Conclusion:** The scattered, dark, irregular necrotic spots on the banana fruit surface, with progressive coalescence into larger decay areas, are classic hallmarks of **Anthracnose** caused by *Colletotrichum musae*.
